public_task_requirement: Please implement a website for a credit repair company to generate leads. The website should have a form-filling function, allowing users to input personal information and credit status. The website should also have a credit score inquiry function and an introduction to credit repair services. Users can browse the website, learn about credit repair services, and fill out the form to submit lead information. Set old lace as the body background and use rosy brown for the UI.

task_summary.requirement_coverage: The site targeted a credit repair lead-generation landing page with three core user-facing capabilities: a form for personal/credit-status lead capture, a credit score inquiry action, and an introduction to credit repair services, all styled with an old lace body background and rosy brown UI. Verified strengths: the credit score inquiry flow was observed to work and display a score/feedback; the color palette was judged to match the requested scheme; the page rendered without visible runtime errors. Main functional risks: the lead form was not confirmed as submitted before interaction budget exhaustion, so the confirmation state was not reached; the services/introduction content was not fully verified and was reported as not found in the interaction trace; navigation/content visibility depended on switching views, which limited confirmation of the required landing-page coverage. Visible observations: the homepage showed navigation buttons, a credit score CTA, and a lead form available on another view, but the screenshot-based review noted that the first screen did not visibly present all required sections together.
verified_strengths: Credit score inquiry was confirmed to display a score and qualitative feedback after the inquiry action.
The requested old lace background and rosy brown UI styling were observed as matching the specification.
The page rendered cleanly with no visible errors in the evaluated screenshot.
primary_functional_risks: Form submission was not reached before the interaction budget ended, so lead-record confirmation remained unverified.
The introduction to credit repair services was not confirmed in the interaction trace and was reported as not visible/found during review.
Because the site uses separate views, required content may not be visible on the initial landing screen without navigation.
primary_visual_observations: The landing page uses a soft light background with rosy brown navigation/buttons, matching the requested palette.
The first screen shows a simple navigation/header area and a credit score CTA, but not all requested lead-generation sections at once.
Text contrast on the hero area was noted as low in the screenshot-based appearance feedback, reducing readability.

appearance_reflection.observed_result: The homepage renders a single H2 headline, "Welcome to Credit Repair Experts." The page uses white text styling in the shared button and root styles, while the app container sets an oldlace background and the main UI areas use rosybrown. The reviewer specifically noted that the headline text contrast against the background is very low and that the typography is minimal, with room for stronger font weight or contrast.
appearance_reflection.likely_cause_or_limitation: Appearance issue on the first screen: the headline is present, but its contrast and weight are not strong enough to read comfortably against the background. The tester did not report a missing element here; the complaint is about what is visible up front.
appearance_reflection.preventative_action: Make the main headline use a clearly higher-contrast text color and a heavier weight so it remains easy to read against the page background. Verify on the first screen that the primary heading is readable without relying on scrolling or interaction.
appearance_reflection.verification: Open the landing page and check that the top headline is immediately legible at normal viewing distance, with visibly stronger contrast and weight than the surrounding text.
appearance_reflection.transfer_limits: Applies to landing pages and hero sections where a primary headline sits over a colored page background.

evidence_refs.same_fix: Increase the text contrast and adjust typography weight so the headline is easier to read against the background.

appearance_reflection.deduction: the contrast between the text ("Welcome to Credit Repair Experts") and the background is very low, making the text hard to read || the typography is minimal but could use some improvements in font weight or contrast for better readability
appearance_reflection.group_reason: Increase the text contrast and adjust typography weight so the headline is easier to read against the background.

functional_reflections.user_trigger: A user fills in the lead form with valid personal information and a credit issue, then submits the form.
functional_reflections.expected_state_change: After submission, the page shows a confirmation message thanking the user and indicating that the lead information was received.
functional_reflections.observed_result: The tester filled in the personal-information fields and selected a credit issue, but did not click the submit button, so no confirmation message was shown.
functional_reflections.likely_cause_or_limitation: (unverified against code) The run ended before the final submit action, so the confirmation state was never exercised.
functional_reflections.preventative_action: For any multi-field form, keep the submit control visible and reachable without extra navigation, and make the post-submit confirmation appear immediately in the same view after the form is submitted. If the form is long, place the submit button at the end of the visible flow or provide a sticky submit action so the final step is not easy to miss.
functional_reflections.verification: Re-run the form flow, enter valid values in all required fields, activate the submit control, and confirm that the success message replaces the form.
functional_reflections.transfer_limits: This lesson applies to form flows that require a final submit action before showing confirmation; it does not address unrelated navigation or content sections.

investigation.task: The check asked to complete the lead form and see a submission confirmation after entering valid personal information and selecting a credit issue. The tester’s final answer was PARTIAL because the submit button was never clicked, so the expected confirmation was not observed.
investigation.reached_target: The tester did reach the form page and filled the personal-information fields, but stopped before the final submit action. Because the form had a visible submit control, the failure is a tester limitation rather than a website defect.
investigation.screenshots: The screenshots show the form page with First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone Number, and the credit-issue dropdown visible and filled. They do not show any post-submit confirmation message, and the submit button is not visible in the captured viewport.
investigation.code_path: src/App.vue contains the route-like view switch and renders FormView when currentView === 'form'. src/views/FormView.vue contains the form and a submit handler that sets submitted = true and swaps the form for a success message, so the feature exists and is wired to show confirmation after submission.
investigation.candidates: 1) Tester limitation: supported by the trajectory and final answer, which explicitly say the submit button was not clicked. 2) Missing confirmation logic: ruled out by src/views/FormView.vue, which sets submitted.value = true and conditionally renders the success message. 3) Unreadable/hidden confirmation: not supported because the confirmation is only shown after submit, and no submit occurred.
investigation.conclusion: The surviving cause is that the tester ran out of interactions before activating the submit button. No website defect is established from the supplied evidence.
investigation.fix_check: No code change is required to explain this check. If the goal is to make the confirmation reachable within the tester’s interaction budget, the form component could expose the submit action more prominently or reduce the number of required pre-submit interactions, but that would not change the fact that this run did not exercise submission.
